q8.answer: Session state lives in the shared Postgres `sessions` table, keyed by sha256 of the session ID (the cookie carries only the raw opaque ID). Either instance hashes the cookie value and queries that table, so no instance holds any session state.

q9.answer: Failed logins are rows in the Postgres `login_failures` table (email, attempted_at, default now()), with an index on (email, attempted_at). The window is decided by counting that email's rows where attempted_at is within the last 10 minutes, using the database clock (now()). Lockouts are in `login_lockouts`.

q10.answer: It runs one atomic UPDATE that matches the hashed ID where last_seen_at is within 30 minutes of now() and created_at is within 12 hours of now(), both using the database clock. If a row matches, it writes last_seen_at = now() (restarting the idle timer) and returns user_id. created_at is never changed.

q11.answer: The browser gets HTTP 503 with the login page showing "Something went wrong. Please try again." The transaction is rolled back, no session is issued, no cookie is set (an existing cookie is left unchanged), and the page does not say whether the credentials were right.

q12.answer: A cleanup job that runs on each instance every 10 minutes deletes sessions with last_seen_at older than 30 minutes or created_at older than 12 hours. It also deletes old login_failures and expired lockouts. Correctness does not depend on it, because expiry is also enforced on every read; the job only reclaims space.
